calls.head: Something has to give
calls.body: The Stars are the league’s best for chance quality, and the Blues are near the top of the league at preventing dangerous shots. We think the Stars still get theirs.
calls.call: The Stars’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Blues.
calls.nums: Dallas 1st for chance quality (a 7.0% chance of scoring on the average shot) · St. Louis 6th for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On chance quality, Dallas had 5.3% a shot. The league average is 6.3% a shot, and they came in at 7.0% a shot.

calls.head: Bring a pillow
calls.body: St. Louis plays some of the league’s slowest games, and so does Dallas. We think this one is even quieter than either team’s usual.
calls.call: The game runs at fewer than 75.1 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, slower than either team’s usual.
calls.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): St. Louis 30th (78.6), Dallas 32nd (75.1)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 67.7 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the slower team’s usual 75.1 and a league average of 81.9.

calls.head: The Stars’ power play outclasses the Blues’
calls.body: On the power play, Dallas is one of the league’s best and St. Louis is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Stars’ power play creates more per 60 than the Blues’.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On power-play expected goals per 60, Dallas had 7.1 per 60 and St. Louis 3.7 per 60. Coming in, Dallas was at 8.7 per 60 and St. Louis at 6.3 per 60.

DAL.head: We had this close to even (50% for Dallas), and it went St. Louis’s way.

STL.head: We had this close to even (50% for St. Louis), and St. Louis came through.

surprises.head: St. Louis got the good looks
surprises.body: St. Louis’s shots at 5-on-5 were more dangerous than usual: a 10.3% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.7% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 100 games.

surprises.head: J. Hofer stole one
surprises.body: J. Hofer allowed 0 goals on shots worth 2.8 expected goals, 2.8 fewer than expected. Starting goalies had a night this good about once every 45 starts over the last three seasons.

story.head: Hofer shuts out the Stars
paras: Mason McTavish opened the scoring 1:34 in. Four different Blues scored. Joel Hofer stopped all 25 shots.
The chances were closer than the score.

items.text: Two of the preview’s three calls held.
